scope: Exactly the68 v136 valid-score noncash episodes; no excluded61 or121 cash-ending rows reintroduced.

empty_candidate_overlap.meaning: Two simultaneous observations: empty designated candidate and recorded closure reason. Not causal attribution of every empty patch to its closure condition.

code_correct_delivery_missing_overlap.meaning: The final selected code was correct, delivery was not accepted, and the shared pool reached its admission boundary. More budget effectiveness was not tested.

pipeline_contract_blocked.headroom_definition: 5,000,000 minus accounted actual input+output tokens; not an API cash balance, reserved token allowance, or proof another action was currently legal.

conclusions_and_limits: Budget and collaboration bottlenecks can reinforce one another: more organizational actions consume shared resources, and reaching the token boundary cuts off further repair/closure attempts.
All12 code-correct but delivery-failed episodes reached the5M boundary; this supports a budget/closure association, not proof that extra tokens would complete delivery.
Only12 of20 empty candidates ended at the token boundary; the other8 ended in organization_contract_blocked. An all-budget explanation is contradicted by the recorded end states.

The12 PIPELINE blocked episodes retained substantial nominal token headroom, and3 already passed both endpoints. The block label means no eligible next organizational step, not uniformly unfinished or failed code.
No timestamp analysis of when the code first became correct was performed; token is total across all members, not a separate allowance each agent can spend.
Rows can overlap across failure mechanisms, but an empty baseline failure is not also a code-passed delivery deficit. Statistics do not estimate an isolated causal budget effect.
This selection excludes cash-ending episodes; these findings do not estimate the influence of monetary cutoff on the complete original250 panel.
